Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:145058
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 28440 of 2023

Applicant :- Vinod
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Nanhe Lal Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA apprised the Court that on 7.6.2023 notice has been served to the informant.
Despite service of notice none present on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri Nanhe Lal Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Jhamman Ram, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
200 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Talbehat Lalitpur, District Lalitpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and one unknown person under section 363 IPC and according to the FIR applicant with the help of the unknown person enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 15 years.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that from the statement of the victim recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it appears that she is major aged about 18 years and she according to her own wish had gone alongwith the applicant and she after performing marriage with the applicant started living with him and she has also become pregnant with him.

6. He further submitted that even as per school record, age of the victim was more than 17 years and victim in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. categorically stated that her age is not 15 years but 18 years.
He next submitted that applicant is also aged about 18 years and it is a case of teenage love.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that even according to the school record, age of the victim is more than 17 years and she in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. categorically stated that her age is 18 years and in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., she did not make any allegation against the applicant.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Even from the school record, it appears that victim is more than 17 years old and she in her both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. stated that her age is 18 years and she is major and from both the statements, it reflects that she according to her own wish had gone alongwith the applicant and performed marriage with him and she also become pregnant with him.
10. Further, from her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., it also reflects that applicant is also around the age of 18 years, therefore, it appears to be the case of teenage love.

11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant-Vinod, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
